title: Подозрительно добрый Шеф  (A Suspiciously Kind Chef)

segments.t: Huddled together in the kitchen, the cooks try to figure out why Chef Barinov is suddenly so polite, sober, and forgiving this morning. Since Spartak lost and the Chef has not touched a drop of alcohol, Fedya convinces the team that something serious must be wrong.
Слушайте, что-то шеф какой-то сегодня слишком добрый.
Просто человек нажрался с утра, и все.
Ну, есть у меня один знакомый, он рассказывал.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'We are just friends.' Barinov maintains a wry tone as they talk, combining "prosto" ("just") and "druzhim" ("be friends") so the key meaning lands right away.
'Nothing at all.' Max brings a steady direction in front of Barinov, weaving "da" ("yes") together with "nichego" ("nothing") just the way native speakers do.
'Well, friendship is a wonderful thing.' Barinov favors a natural course with Max, building the phrase around "druzhba" ("friendship") and "prekrasno" ("perfectly") for a crisp, natural delivery.
Слушайте, что-то шеф какой-то сегодня слишком добрый.
'Listen, the Chef is being way too kind today.' Max presents a lively stance as they talk, pairing "slushayte" ("listen") with "segodnya" ("today") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'That does not bode well.' Barinov maintains a direct note right away, putting "dobru" ("good, kindness") alongside "vot" ("there, here") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'Maybe Spartak won?' Max probes warmly during the talk, pairing "mozhet" ("can") with "vyigrali" ("won") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'No, it looks like they lost.' Barinov shares a steady attitude right away, putting "proigral" ("lost") alongside "da" ("yes") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
Просто человек нажрался с утра, и все.

'The man simply got wasted first thing in the morning, that is all.' Max keeps an earnest tempo with Barinov, weaving "prosto" ("just") together with "chelovek" ("a man, a person") just the way native speakers do.
'No, he seemed completely sober.' Barinov strikes a resolute course with Max, building the phrase around "trezvyy" ("sober") and "byl" ("was") for a crisp, natural delivery.
'Something else is going on here.' Max conveys a thoughtful bearing with Barinov, building the phrase around "tut" ("here") and "drugoye" ("another, other") for a crisp, natural delivery.
'How do you even know about that?' Barinov probes honestly toward Max here, putting "otkuda" ("where from") alongside "znayesh" ("know") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
Ну, есть у меня один знакомый, он рассказывал.
'Well, I have an acquaintance who told me all about it.' Max offers a clear tack in this beat, leaning on "yest" ("there is") before closing the thought with "znakomyy" ("familiar").
'Anyway, look here.' Barinov picks a thoughtful tone in this beat, anchoring the Russian line on "koroche" ("long story short") and "smotrite" ("look") without extra filler.
Слушайте, что-то шеф какой-то сегодня слишком добрый.
Просто человек нажрался с утра, и все.
Ну, есть у меня один знакомый, он рассказывал.
That wraps up this scene as the cooks gather to figure out why Chef Barinov is acting so unusually gentle and sober this morning, suspecting a secret diagnosis or crisis. Until next time!
